Explicitly scoped to the probed state and horizon: an instantaneous braking-box input at the saved update-34 projected state produced endpoint tip speed 0.6129798468327005 m/s versus 0.6155277254823904 m/s under the recorded actual_tension_n, i.e. no material endpoint-speed gain at 10 ms, so the recorded terminal command did not leave local endpoint-speed-reduction authority unused at this state; the large deceleration-along-velocity contrast (891.7363309396493 vs 22.297467181011292 m/s^2) accompanies a velocity-direction change, not a large endpoint speed difference. This does not rule out braking authority at other saved states or over longer horizons.

Within this bounded probe the recorded actual_tension_n already delivered an endpoint tip speed essentially equal to the braking-box arm's at the same saved state and fixed 0.01 s horizon, so the local commanded input is not the limiting factor at update 34; the residual speed excess recorded in the settling window is therefore not explained at this state by an un-braked terminal command. Scope: one saved projected state, projected model, advisory-only.

The two arms differ more in position response (position drift 0.006487739485323485 m vs 0.004113715254212544 m; braking-box arm endpoint tip error 0.009868288776480223 m, close to the 0.01 m position limit) and in endpoint velocity direction ([-0.31449254261532283, 0.4680237960169863, -0.24040062317772942] m/s) than in scalar endpoint speed, so at this state a locally maximal braking input trades tip position/direction against speed rather than buying endpoint-speed margin; a single-state 10 ms read cannot rank this against planning-level mechanisms.

The recorded weights are speed-light (terminal_tip_speed_weight 0.0, velocity_weight and terminal_velocity_weight 0.0001 versus tracking_weight 1.0, terminal_weight 5.0), but raw magnitudes do not establish cost-term importance because no cost contributions or scaling are retained; the completed probe additionally weakens the local form of this candidate by showing that a braking-box input bought no material endpoint speed reduction at update 34 over 10 ms, so this candidate is neither supported at the probed state nor excluded over planning timescales and the full window.

Effective horizon fell 8 -> 1 control intervals across updates 27-34 and displayed late updates ended with User_Requested_Stop, which is compatible with budget-limited selection; the probe was run at a single recorded state using the recorded input and cannot separate plan selection or horizon effects from objective weighting whenever they predict the same endpoint, and per-iteration traces and full warm plans are not retained, so this stays possible and unranked.

Recorded GVS projection residuals of 2.3741307545542503-2.500592461937906 rad/m indicate ongoing model disagreement, but the completed probe used the same projected model and a recorded projected GVS state, not the complete backend state, so it cannot bound backend-model mismatch; a 10 ms projected-model probe cannot explain an entire settling failure and no closed-loop replay capability exists.
